jetting.rule: Hold AFR constant: A_jet ∝ sqrt(rho_air), so d_jet ∝ rho^0.25. Target area = A_ref * sqrt(rho/rho_ref). Map area to a jet number using measured diameters (about 2% area per number); snap to the nearest available size; round toward the larger (richer) jet; clamp to the legal max of the active rule layers.
jetting.derivation: m_f = Cd*A_j*sqrt(2*rho_f*dp); dp ≈ m_a^2/(2*rho_a*A_v^2), so sqrt(dp) ∝ m_a/sqrt(rho_a); AFR = m_a/m_f ∝ sqrt(rho_a)/A_j; constant AFR gives A_j ∝ sqrt(rho_a). Standard atmosphere: about -2.9% density per 1000 ft. Gives about 0.4-0.7 jet numbers per 1000 ft DA and about 0.3-0.5 numbers per 10 °F.

alternative_rule.value: Longacre: change jet area by the same % as air density (A ∝ rho), about twice the sqrt rule (about 0.9-1.4 numbers per 1000 ft).
alternative_rule.notes: Recorded as a conflict, not averaged. sqrt rule is the default because it changes the jet less (safer when air thins).

jetting.table_notes: Illustration only (sqrt rule, nominal diameters, hypothetical reference of 58 at 0 ft). Not a published table.

direction.value: lower density (heat, altitude, low pressure, humidity) richens the mixture, so use a smaller jet; cold dense air leans it, so use a larger jet

symptoms.signs: Sluggish, lugging off corners, sputter, smoke, wet black plug, oil spitting from the exhaust
symptoms.fix: First rule out choke, dirty filter and fouled plug; then one jet size smaller

symptoms.signs: Four-stroking (uneven blubbering) at full throttle or top speed; flat top end
symptoms.fix: One jet size smaller, checked with a plug chop

symptoms.signs: Over-revs or 'screams' then goes flat, sharp popping or pinging, overheating, white or grey chalky plug; seizure risk
symptoms.fix: Go one jet size LARGER right away; check intake air leaks, float and needle valve, fuel line and filter. Never lean out to chase speed.

symptoms.signs: Hesitates or nearly dies when the throttle is snapped open, then surges
Needs choke to idle; dies when the throttle closes
symptoms.fix: Clean the idle hole and spray tube; check the float and needle valve and for intake leaks. Not a jet change.

symptoms.signs: Light to dark tan or chocolate is good; white or grey is lean (or plug too hot); black and wet is rich. Read after a full-throttle plug chop; castor two-stroke plugs are hard to read; EGT is preferred.
symptoms.fix: Use as a sanity check for main jet changes

quirks.text: Axle diameter differs between sources: 25 mm (older spec, 25x950x3 part) vs 30 mm (2026 product page). Bearings, hubs and cassettes are not interchangeable between them; measure before ordering or recommending hub changes.
The D.17 spindle type used on Mini and Kid Kart is listed as discontinued.
Kid kart tire wear dots often do not touch the ground; do not use them to judge pressure.
Kid kart tires are hard and the kart is light, so they build little heat; forum practice is to run near the 20 psi cap and bleed to ~19-19.5 after warm-up.
For 5-8 year-olds, a predictable, easy-to-drive kart (neither loose nor pushing) and a correct seat position matter more than fine tuning.
TopKart USA parts were reported ~3 days out in the USA.
